questions.prompt: Explain how a recipe PATCH replaces its ingredient list, what the three payload cases do, and why validation must come first.

keyPoints.text: Replacing children wholesale is simpler and safer than diffing rows, because the editor sends the full list.
keyPoints.quote: replacing children wholesale is easier to get right than diffing rows

keyPoints.text: An omitted ingredients key leaves existing rows untouched.
An explicit empty array removes every ingredient, on purpose.
Validation must run before the delete, or a typo would wipe a valid recipe.
keyPoints.quote: a typo would wipe an otherwise valid recipe

keyPoints.text: Ingredient ids change on every save, which is acceptable only because nothing references them.
keyPoints.quote: Ingredient ids are **not stable** across edits

keyPoints.text: The server's own blank-row check matters for API callers, not just the editor's filter.
keyPoints.quote: The server check is the one that matters for API callers.

questions.prompt: Why is the tiny tx() helper correct with node:sqlite, what can it not cover, and how do the delete handlers deal with that?

keyPoints.text: The driver is synchronous, so the callback cannot await and nothing interleaves.
keyPoints.quote: `fn` cannot `await`, so no other request can run between `BEGIN` and `COMMIT` in this process

keyPoints.text: An async driver would need a dedicated client per transaction.
keyPoints.quote: the same helper would need a dedicated client per transaction

keyPoints.text: The helper is not re-entrant: nesting would issue a second BEGIN and fail.
keyPoints.quote: cannot start a transaction within a transaction

keyPoints.text: A transaction cannot cover files on disk.
keyPoints.quote: What it cannot cover: files on disk.

keyPoints.text: Dish and recipe deletes collect filenames inside the transaction and delete files after commit.
The cook-log delete removes photo files inside the transaction instead.

questions.prompt: How is search kept in sync with the source tables, and how is user text turned into a safe, well-ranked FTS5 query?

keyPoints.text: There are no triggers; each handler calls a re-indexer.
Each re-indexer deletes its row and rebuilds it from the source tables.
keyPoints.quote: delete my row, rebuild it from source

keyPoints.text: A cook log's search title embeds the recipe title, so a recipe rename must re-index its cook logs.
keyPoints.quote: renaming a recipe must re-index every cook log under it

keyPoints.text: Dish renames do not cascade because dish names are resolved at query time.
keyPoints.quote: dish names are resolved live at query time

keyPoints.text: User text never reaches MATCH raw: it always passes through toFtsQuery (queries.ts lines 175-183) first.
Title hits are weighted ten times body hits.
keyPoints.quote: weights a title hit ten times a body hit

keyPoints.text: A query that still fails to parse yields no results rather than a server error.
